source.title: Momentum Centering and Asynchronous Update for Adaptive Gradient Methods
source.authors: Juntang Zhuang; Yifan Ding; Tommy M. Tang; N. Dvornek; S. Tatikonda; James S. Duncan

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out image-classification performance using its own training experiments; this is a different optimizer comparison from the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The convergence examples and cited results are not rows. Included the paper’s own held-out optimizer comparisons; table values are reported as stated, and figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-10 experiments directly compare held-out accuracy of adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD. They bear on V4, although tuning includes epsilon and the principal adaptive optimizer is newly proposed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the empirical conclusion: the authors claim ACProp generalizes like SGD, converges quickly and trains stably like Adam, and often outperforms Adam and AdaBelief. They also conclude that it has weaker convergence conditions and an optimal stochastic nonconvex convergence rate.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a new asynchronous centered adaptive optimizer against SGD and other optimizers; it does not test the original claim’s random-label or generalization-gap interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer performance varies by model and task; ACProp is more sensitive to β2 than β1, as reported in Appendix C.2.

fits_no_version.finding: ACProp exceeds Adam's translation BLEU on all four tasks; all compared optimizers are adaptive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizer design affects translation performance, with ACProp outperforming tuned Adam in these experiments.

record.problems: The central optimizer comparison reports test accuracy in Figure 7 without numerical values in the text. Table 2 mixes study results with values attributed to external sources. Transformer table reports BLEU scores but does not include an SGD comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional held-out optimizer comparison rows were omitted; convergence examples, GAN and reinforcement-learning metrics do not measure the image-classification or language held-out comparison in V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

A limited-tuning versus broader-tuning intervention; matched training performance underlying held-out differences; SGD comparisons on language tasks; word-level language modeling; switching optimizers; and an isolated decoupled-weight-decay intervention.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.

missing.what: Separate momentum-SGD versus Adam, AdamW, RAdam, AdaBelief and AdaShift comparisons for each CIFAR-10 architecture. The ACProp-centered rows omit these direct V4 comparisons. Figure 24 also supplies corresponding training accuracy; their directions and numerical values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
missing.locator: Figures 7 and 24; Section 5 and Appendix C.2

record.verdict_notes: Reversed states for R1–R3 refer to the adaptive-versus-SGD penalty, not to every clause of V4. ImageNet's mixed-source table does not warrant a separate verdict. Translation improvements over Adam do not support an adaptive-versus-SGD claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The study does not report word-level language-model results, switching from Adam to SGD, or a controlled comparison isolating weight decay. Its image-classification comparison uses extensive hyperparameter tuning; the cited SGD ImageNet accuracy is not the study’s own run.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 VGG-11, ResNet-34 and DenseNet-121, using ACProp with extensive optimizer tuning
relationships.reason: R1–R3 report that the adaptive optimizer ACProp outperforms momentum SGD, showing that an adaptive-method penalty does not extend to this optimizer and tuning setting; this does not establish that extra tuning alone removed a penalty.
relationships.display_finding: ACProp reportedly outperformed momentum SGD across the tested architectures, but these comparisons remain unverified and do not isolate tuning's contribution.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
